sentences.text: Netram vs State Of U.P. on 12 December, 2019
Author: Pradeep Kumar Srivastava
Bench: Pradeep Kumar Srivastava HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD ?Court No. - 55 Case :- CRIMINAL REVISION No. - 644 of 2003 Revisionist :- Netram Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

entities.text: HIGH COURT OF JUDICATURE AT ALLAHABAD
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Counsel for Revisionist :- G.R.S. Pal Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt.Advocate Hon'ble Pradeep Kumar Srivastava,J.
None present even in the revised list from the side of revisionist.
Shri Ravi Kant Kushwaha and Shri Chavi Pal Singh, learned A.G.As are present.
Heard on revision.

Order sheet shows that in pursuance of the order sheet dated 12.02.2016, notice was issued to the revisionist to engage another counsel which was served personally as reported by the office on 11.12.2019.
It is also pertinent to mention that in-charge C.J.M, Badaun by his letter dated 11.03.2016 has reported that the notice was served on the revisionist personally.
This revision is of year 2003.

Netram vs State Of U.P. on 12 December, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105814664/
1

This criminal revision has been filed against the judgement and order dated 04.09.2000 passed by A.C.J.M-Ist, Badaun in Criminal Case No. 4018 of 1993 under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, convicting the revisionist who undergoes six months rigorous imprisonment and fine of Rs. 1,000/- and in default one month simple imprisonment.

Against conviction and sentence the revisionist preferred appeal before the Sessions Court which was numbered as Criminal Appeal no. 55 of 2000 and the Sessions Judge vide order dated 25.02.2003 dismissed the appeal and upheld the conviction and sentence passed by the learned trial court.
From the perusal of the order dated 05.03.2003, it appears that the revisionist was released on bail and the fine was also stayed.

From the perusal of both the impugned judgements, it appears that both the courts arrived on the finding that sample of milk was taken from the revisionist, applying due procedure and the same was sent for chemical examination only.
On the basis of standard prescribed, the sample was found to be adulterated.

Both the courts arrived at the conclusion that there was nothing on the record to contradict the prosecution case and the witnesses examined in support of prosecution supported the version of complaint.
Very strangely, the revisionist, during trial, did not take recourse of re-examination of the sampled milk after receipt of chemical examination.
The learned trial court finding the accused revisionist guilty for the said offence has awarded minimum sentence prescribed for the offence under Section 7/16 Prevention of Food Adulteration Act.

The impugned orders have been challenged and on the ground that the sentence is too much and is against the law and is not passed on evidence on record and the trial court and the appellate court did not consider the evidence properly.
I did not find any force in the ground taken by the revisionist as both the courts below have passed the judgement on the basis of evidence on record and minimum sentence has been awarded.
When there is concurrent findings of the two courts below, there appears to be no possibility of any material irregularity or illegality or any jurisdictional error.
In view of the above, I find no force in the revision.
The revision is dismissed.
The bail of the revisionist passed vide order dated 05.03.2003 is cancelled and sureties are discharge.
Stay order, if any, is vacated.

Revisionist Netram (convicted accused) shall either surrender forthwith to under go the sentence and if he does not surrender before the court below, he shall be arrested and sent to jail for under going the sentence.
Copy of this judgement be sent to the concerned court for information and necessary compliance.

Order Date :- 12.12.2019 PS  Netram vs State Of U.P. on 12 December, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/105814664/
